headline: Shishir Kumar Bajoria Files SEBI Takeover Disclosure for IFGL Refractories
sum: Shishir Kumar Bajoria has filed a substantial acquisition disclosure under SEBI Takeover Regulations Regulation 31(4) in relation to IFGL Refractories Limited, signalling a potential open offer or significant shareholding acquisition triggering mandatory disclosure and public offer requirements.
detail: Under SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011, Regulation 31(4) requires disclosure of the acquisition of shares or voting rights that trigger a mandatory open offer threshold. Shishir Kumar Bajoria's filing indicates he has crossed or is approaching the 25% threshold (or such other prescribed threshold) that mandates a public offer to all shareholders on an equal basis. The disclosure triggers a series of statutory approvals and timelines, including board constitution of an independent committee, valuation by independent evaluator, and public offer announcement within the prescribed regulatory window.

structure.novel: Regulation 31(4) disclosure is a procedural landmark: it is the earliest formal intimation to market of a mandatory open offer sequence, immediately triggering independent committee constitution and valuation processes. The disclosure itself does not require a specific offer price announcement, but signals intent and locks acquirer into SEBI timeline.

triggers.law: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011, Regulation 31(4)
triggers.note: Disclosure trigger: when acquirer crosses 25% (or prescribed threshold), must disclose within 2 calendar days; failure to disclose is violation attracting monetary penalties and trading suspension.
Open offer mandatory trigger: acquisition of 25%+ in listed company mandates public offer on equal terms to all shareholders; non-compliance results in SEBI enforcement and forced divestment orders.

Independent committee trigger: target board must constitute committee of independent directors to evaluate acquisition proposal; committee's recommendation materially influences offer acceptance rates and regulatory scrutiny.
